name: Aus
seed_requirement_per_acre: 28-37 kg in case of broadcasting: 14-19 kg in case of line sowing
favourable_temperature: Ideal temperature range: 20°C to 36°C (average day temperature) with 20°C to 23°C (night temperature). Tolerance: Can tolerate 19°C to 40°C. Specific stages: Germination: Minimum 10°C. Flowering: 22°C to 23°C. Grain formation: 20°C to 21°C. Mean air temperature for growth: Around 22°C.
favourable_humidity: Higher relative humidity (%) within the crop canopy is usually conducive for growth, particularly in the kharif season when humidity is high.
photo_period: Total accumulated sunshine hours: 1000 hours during the crop span. Last 30 days: 220 to 240 hours of sunshine are ideal for maximum yield.
favourable_rainfall: Optimum rainfall range: 1120 mm to 1500 mm during the 4-month growing period. Standing water: Essential from tillering to grain ripening. The crop is highly sensitive to water deficiency at the flowering and heading stages.
water_requirement: Total water requirement: 80 to 180 cm (depending on crop variety, local climate, growing season, and soil type). During the kharif season, continuous submergence is not essential due to high humidity and low evaporative demands, but it is required in the rabi season.

name: Boro
favourable_temperature: Ideal growth temperatures: 20°C to 36°C during the day, 20°C to 23°C at night. Tolerance range: 19°C to 40°C. Specific stages: Germination: At least 10°C. Flowering: 22°C to 23°C. Grain formation: 20°C to 21°C. Mean air temperature: 22°C is required for overall growth.
favourable_humidity: Higher relative humidity within the crop canopy is conducive for growth, especially during the kharif season when humidity is typically high.
favourable_soil_temperature: Above 16°C is essential after transplanting for successful growth.
photo_period: Total accumulated sunshine hours: 1000 hours during the crop span. Last 30 days: 220 to 240 hours of sunshine.
favourable_rainfall: Optimum rainfall: 1120 mm to 1500 mm over the 4-month growing period. Standing water from tillering to grain ripening is beneficial. Rice is highly sensitive to water deficiency at flowering and heading stages.
water_requirement: Total water requirement: 80 to 180 cm depending on crop variety, climate, growing season, and soil type. Continuous submergence is not always necessary in the kharif season, but it is crucial in the rabi season due to lower humidity.

name: Aman
favourable_temperature: Ideal growth temperatures: 20°C to 36°C (day), 20°C to 23°C (night). Tolerance range: 19°C to 40°C. Specific stages: Germination: Minimum 10°C. Flowering: 22°C to 23°C. Grain formation: 20°C to 21°C. Mean air temperature for growth: Around 22°C.
favourable_humidity: Higher relative humidity (RH%) within the crop canopy is conducive, especially in the kharif season where humidity is naturally higher.
photo_period: Total accumulated sunshine hours: 1000 hours during the crop span. Last 30 days: 220 to 240 hours of sunshine.
favourable_rainfall: Optimum rainfall: 1120 mm to 1500 mm (well-distributed over the 4-month growing period). Standing water is important from tillering to grain ripening. Rice is highly sensitive to water deficiency during the flowering and heading stages.
water_requirement: Total water requirement: 80 to 180 cm (varies with crop variety, climate, growing season, and soil type). Kharif season: Continuous submergence is not always required due to high humidity and low evaporative demands. Rabi season: Continuous submergence is crucial to meet the water demands. Water-saving techniques: Adopting suitable irrigation methods can help reduce water losses.

name: Wheat
seed_requirement_per_acre: (a) 28-33 kg if sown without irrigation. (b) 33-37 kg if sown with 1-2 times irrigation. (c) 37-47 kg if sown with 4-5times irrigation.
favourable_temperature: Optimal temperature for growth and development: 15°C to 20°C. Tolerance: Can withstand intense cold conditions but is sensitive to high temperatures. Detrimental high temperatures: 30°C to 35°C. Specific stages: Germination (Winter Wheat): Optimal temperature is 15°C to 20°C. Cardinal temperatures for germination: Minimum: 3°C to 4.5°C. Optimum: Around 25°C. Maximum: 30°C to 32°C. Effects of high temperature: Poor tillering, lower number of effective tillers, short shoot height, smaller ears, lower grain weight and quality.
favourable_humidity: The crop benefits from bright sunny days with dryness and cooler nights during ripening for better grain size and quality.
favourable_soil_temperature: High soil moisture content is important for high germination rates, good seedling establishment, and proper seed setting and development. Wheat is drought resistant but highly sensitive to moisture stress during critical growth stages, particularly from shooting to heading.
photo_period: Bright, sunny days during the ripening period enhance grain quality.
favourable_rainfall: Optimum rainfall: 50 cm to 87.5 cm during the growing season. Total water requirement: 45 cm to 55 cm (varies by variety and seasonal conditions). Daily consumptive use (CU): Varies from 0.17 cm to 0.87 cm from emergence to grain filling, peaking at 0.62 cm during boot to dough stages.
water_requirement: The crop requires adequate water during critical stages, especially in areas with limited water supply. Managing water during these critical stages is important for good crop performance.

name: Maize
favourable_temperature: Ideal mean temperature for growth: 24°C with night temperatures above 15°C. No maize cultivation possible if the mean summer temperature is below 19°C or if the average night temperature during the three summer months falls below 21°C. High temperatures: If the maximum temperature exceeds 35°C during the flowering period, fertilization will be hampered, resulting in poor yield. High night temperatures can also lead to lower yields.
favourable_humidity: Maize is adapted to a warm and humid climate, with moderate water needs depending on the type of soil and the season.
favourable_soil_temperature: Minimum soil temperature: Maize seeds begin to germinate at a soil temperature of around 10°C (50°F), but germination will be slow. Optimal soil temperature: The ideal soil temperature for maize germination is between 16°C to 35°C (60°F to 95°F). Within this range, germination is faster and more uniform.
photo_period: The photoperiod is longer, but as modern varieties are day-neutral, this does not impact growth as significantly as with traditional varieties.
favourable_rainfall: Optimum rainfall requirement: 50 cm to 75 cm. Water requirement: High during the inflorescence stage.
water_requirement: Water requirements vary depending on the soil type and season, but excess water during the growing period should be avoided as maize is highly sensitive to waterlogging.

name: Potato
favourable_temperature: Optimal temperatures for different growth stages: Spouting: 18°C to 21°C. Seedling to vegetative growth: 10°C to 18°C. Tuber setting and bulking: Day temperatures of 18°C to 20°C and night temperatures below 15°C.
favourable_humidity: Optimal relative humidity is 65% to 80%, especially for maintaining soil moisture at 65-80% of field capacity.
favourable_soil_temperature: Optimum soil temperature: 15°C to 18°C for potato growth during different stages.
photo_period: At least 6 to 9 hours of sunshine are required for optimal potato production.
favourable_rainfall: Optimal rainfall requirement: 400 mm to 600 mm during the growing period. Water requirement: 400 mm to 450 mm for different varieties, depending on growth stages. Rainfall sensitivity: Heavy rains and alternating dry/wet spells can be harmful.
water_requirement: Moderate water needs: Potatoes do not require very high water. Well-distributed rainfall during the vegetative period is important.

name: Lentil
favourable_temperature: For germination and vegetative stages: Optimal temperature: 10°C to 21.15°C. Harmful temperature: Below 10°C and above 24°C can negatively affect germination. For flowering and pod initiation stages: Optimal temperature: 14°C to 25°C. Harmful temperature: Temperatures above 32°C negatively impact flowering and pod initiation.
favourable_humidity: For germination and vegetative stages: 50% to 90%. For flowering and pod initiation stages: 45% to 75%.
favourable_soil_temperature: At least 5°C to 12.8°C is required for proper growth.
photo_period: Lentil requires 11.2 to 11.4 hours of daylight during its life cycle for optimal growth.
favourable_rainfall: 100 mm (average water requirement across growth phases)
water_requirement: An average of 100 mm of water is required during its different growing phases.

name: Mung
favourable_temperature: Optimum growth: 25-35 °C Sensitive to frost; temperatures below 10 °C can adversely affect growth.
photo_period: Mung beans are generally day-neutral but can benefit from longer daylight hours.
favourable_rainfall: Approximately 500-800 mm is optimal for growth; however, they can tolerate drought conditions once established.
water_requirement: Mung beans require about 300-400 mm of water throughout their growing cycle, depending on the soil and climate conditions.

name: Gram
favourable_temperature: Optimum growth: 20-30 °C Sensitive to frost; temperatures below 10 °C can hinder germination and growth.
favourable_soil_temperature: Ideal range is 15-25 °C for optimal germination and growth.
photo_period: Chickpeas are generally day-neutral but perform better with longer daylight hours.
favourable_rainfall: Approximately 600-800 mm is required during the growing season.
water_requirement: Chickpeas need around 300-400 mm of water throughout their growth cycle, with tolerance to dry conditions once established.

name: Mustard
favourable_temperature: Optimum growth: 15-25 °C Temperatures above 30 °C can adversely affect flowering and seed development.
favourable_soil_temperature: Ideal range is 10-20 °C for optimal germination.
photo_period: Mustard is generally short-day sensitive, thriving with shorter daylight hours during its flowering stage.
favourable_rainfall: Approximately 500-700 mm is needed during the growing season.
water_requirement: Mustard requires about 300-400 mm of water throughout its growth cycle.

name: Groundnut
favourable_temperature: Optimum growth: 24-34 °C Harmful Temperatures: Above 34 °C and below 14 °C Optimum seed germination temperature: 14-16 °C
favourable_humidity: High atmospheric humidity is beneficial for flowering and peg setting.
favourable_soil_temperature: Ideal mean soil temperature for pod formation: 23 °C Low soil temperatures can retard germination and plant growth.
photo_period: Groundnuts typically require full sunlight for optimal growth.
favourable_rainfall: Approximately 500-700 mm of well-distributed rainfall is adequate for the crop.
water_requirement: Moist soil conditions are critical from emergence to flowering. Dry conditions are needed for pod maturity and harvesting. Moisture stress during the vegetative period can delay flowering and reduce yield.

name: Chili
favourable_temperature: Optimum growth: 20-30 °C Temperatures above 35 °C can negatively impact flowering and fruit set.
favourable_soil_temperature: Ideal range is 20-30 °C for optimal germination and growth.
photo_period: Chili plants are day-length sensitive, thriving in longer daylight hours, especially during flowering.
favourable_rainfall: Approximately 800-1200 mm is required during the growing season, with good distribution to avoid drought stress.
water_requirement: Chili requires consistent moisture, especially during flowering and fruit development, but excessive water can lead to root rot.

name: Onion
seed_requirement_per_acre: 2-3 kg (in case of seeds); 2-3 Ql. (in case of bulb)
favourable_temperature: Optimum growth: 15-25 °C Onions can tolerate temperatures up to 30 °C, but prolonged heat can affect bulb formation.
favourable_soil_temperature: Ideal soil temperature for germination is around 20-25 °C.
photo_period: Onions are day-length sensitive; long days are generally favorable for bulb formation, especially in the summer.
favourable_rainfall: Approximately 500-1000 mm is needed during the growing season, with a focus on well-distributed rainfall.
water_requirement: Onions require consistent moisture, especially during bulb formation; they need about 300-500 mm of water throughout their growth cycle.

name: Garlic
favourable_temperature: Optimum growth: 15-25 °C Garlic can tolerate temperatures up to 30 °C, but excessive heat can affect bulb development.
favourable_soil_temperature: Ideal range is 10-20 °C for optimal germination.
photo_period: Garlic is a long-day plant and benefits from longer daylight hours for bulb formation.
favourable_rainfall: Approximately 600-800 mm is needed during the growing season, ideally with a well-distributed pattern.
water_requirement: Garlic requires consistent moisture, particularly during the bulbing stage, but it is sensitive to waterlogging.

name: Sugarcane
sowing_time: Early Mid October to Mid December
favourable_temperature: Optimum growth: 25-35 °C Favorable for maturity: 12-14 °C Harmful temperature: Above 37 °C inhibits growth
favourable_soil_temperature: Ideal range is 16-32 °C for optimal growth.
photo_period: Long days (average sunshine of 7-9 hours) are necessary for good vegetative growth.
favourable_rainfall: Requires 1250-1650 mm of rainfall annually, with high moisture levels throughout the root zone.
water_requirement: Total water requirement varies between 300-1000 mm across different growth stages. Irrigation is needed when soil moisture depletion reaches 50% (up to 270 days after planting) and 75% depletion requires irrigation after 270 days.

name: Jute
favourable_humidity: Minimum: 60% Optimum: More than 80% is best for growth.
favourable_soil_temperature: Not explicitly mentioned, but generally aligns with the air temperature range.
photo_period: Jute is a short-day length plant.
favourable_rainfall: Requires well-distributed annual rainfall of 1000-1500 mm with bright sunlight.
water_requirement: Cannot withstand waterlogging during the seedling stage; moisture management is crucial.
